root_idea.summary: The root centers on orderly, even arrangement and regularity along a straight course, extending to clear, well-formed articulation and deliberate recitation.
root_idea.development: The lexical orientation develops from the even setting or separation of the teeth and the good arrangement of a thing to speech that is orderly, distinct, easy, and unhurried. In the Qur'anic expression of 25:32, this further carries the idea of successive, deliberate portions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form II perfect citation form.
Displayed as the corresponding verbal noun.

senses.definition: To recite or articulate words distinctly, in an orderly, deliberate, and unhurried manner.
senses.usage_conditions: In Qur'anic use, the construction concerns clear and measured recitation, with the components of the speech properly arranged; attention to articulation and pauses is part of the conventional recitational practice.

senses.definition: To deliver or recite the Qur'an in successive portions, deliberately and over time.
senses.usage_conditions: This specialized interpretation is associated with وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلًا in 25:32, where the Qur'an is understood as being presented part by part; it is not a general synonym for revelation.

senses.definition: Distinct, orderly, deliberate recitation or articulation, without haste.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Qur'anic context especially for recitation characterized by clear utterance, measured pacing, and properly arranged portions of speech.

senses.definition: The deliberate presentation or recitation of the Qur'an in successive portions.
senses.usage_conditions: This constructional sense is specifically attested in the explanation of 25:32, where the Qur'an is delivered or recited part by part over time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Separation or spacing of the teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is described as the original concrete sense associated with the verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deliberate, orderly, and distinct articulation of speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to speech generally, including proceeding through its component parts without haste.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Evenness and good setting of the front teeth, including their being properly separated; also their whiteness and lustre.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related adjectival application may describe a person possessing such teeth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A good, correct, or well-ordered state of arrangement or disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a thing whose component parts are properly arranged.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Describing front teeth that are well set, even in growth, or separated by interstices without overlapping; also describing a person with such teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptions vary among even growth, separation, good setting, whiteness, and lustre.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Speech or language that is good, deliberate, and distinctly uttered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to speech or language rather than restricted to Qur'anic recitation.
Applied broadly to a thing characterized as agreeable or pleasing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A genus of venomous creeping creatures, with several species whose bites cause swelling and pain and may be deadly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later application to the tarantula is reported as possibly incorrect; the lexical item primarily denotes the described venomous creature or genus.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plant with a flower resembling a lily, used medicinally against the bite of the associated venomous creature and against scorpion stings.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man in the cited lexical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a defect or impediment in speech or utterance.
